answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to a costly, verifiable work history instead of free identities. Each agent long-lived record of completed useful tasks emits a signal that is expensive to fake at scale: one forged persona can produce some signal, but a grove of a thousand clones must each earn trust individually, multiplying the real compute and interaction cost on the attacker. Trust then accumulates like a lotus, slow to bloom, so a sybil farm cannot rush it without spending more than its fake identities are ever worth.
